needs: A code walk: lines of a short loop light up while one variable changes value.

brief.title: Walking through a loop, one line at a time
brief.idea: A loop runs the same lines again and again, and following one variable through each pass shows exactly how a running total is built.

beats.say: Here are five lines of Python that add up three prices: four, seven and two.
beats.show: Five lines of code appear: prices = [4, 7, 2], total = 0, for p in prices:, total = total + p, print(total).

beats.say: The list holds the prices. The loop will visit each one, in order, exactly once.
beats.show: The list on line one is highlighted, with its three values marked in order.

beats.say: We will follow one variable, total, and watch its value change as the lines run.
beats.show: An empty box labelled total appears beside the code.

beats.say: The second line sets total to zero, before anything at all has been added to it.
beats.show: Line two is highlighted and the total box shows 0.

beats.say: The loop line picks the first price from the list, so p is now four.
beats.show: Line three is highlighted and a box labelled p appears showing 4.

beats.say: Line four adds p to total. Zero plus four makes four, so total is now four.
beats.show: Line four is highlighted; the total box changes from 0 to 4.

beats.say: Back to the loop line. p becomes seven, and total goes from four to eleven.
beats.show: Line three, then line four, is highlighted; p shows 7 and total changes from 4 to 11.

beats.say: One more pass. p becomes two, and total goes from eleven to thirteen.
beats.show: Lines three and four are highlighted again; p shows 2 and total changes from 11 to 13.

beats.say: No prices are left, so the loop ends, and the last line prints thirteen.
beats.show: Line five is highlighted and 13 appears in an output panel below the code.

beats.say: Line by line, total held zero, then four, then eleven, then thirteen.
beats.show: A short history beside the total box lists 0, 4, 11, 13 in order.

beats.say: Each pass ran the same line, but with a new p, and the total that the last pass left behind.
beats.show: The three passes are shown one above the other, each pairing a value of p with total before and after.

beats.say: Give the list five prices and nothing else in the code changes. The loop simply runs five times.
beats.show: The list grows to five values and a counter beside the loop line reads 5 passes.
